evidence.snippet: 1. When `melian compare adjudicate` judges an external finding `valid` and no match names it, Melian copies its evidence. A Melian finding, a matched external finding and any other verdict keep nothing.

Until [issue #627](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/627) builds the prune, the remedy is to raise `evidence.budget`. Melian's store is never deleted by hand, so neither the refusal nor any document tells a person to remove evidence.

lowered.reason: The stale evidence is genuine, and `print` does not claim a verdict. The budget refusal needs a 1 GiB directory and is fixed by raising `evidence.budget`, as decision items 6 and 8 and the 'What this gives up' section describe. The decision does not require removing evidence when a verdict changes.

verification.reason: The code does what the claim says. adjudicateComparison copies evidence only when the verdict is valid and no match exists. Nothing in EvidenceStore removes files: a search of packages/pipeline/src/evidence.ts for remove, unlink or rm finds nothing. `CloneEvidence.print` reads the pointer without checking the current verdict or match. So evidence kept for a miss later re-judged noise or matched stays readable and still counts toward `held` against the budget. The harm is narrower than the P2 label says. Decision item 1 says "any other verdict keep[s] nothing", which describes what that adjudication copies. It does not say to delete evidence kept earlier. The output never claims the finding is still valid, and the evidence is still a true record of the round. The budget exhaustion needs the directory to reach the budget (1 GiB by default), and the decision's remedy for that is to raise `evidence.budget`. Deleting evidence on re-judgement would be a new feature that the decision's "never deleted by hand" and durable-directory stance does not call for. Only a real run could show whether the stale evidence confuses anyone in practice.

evidence.snippet: It keeps everything else, `tools/` included, and lists every name it leaves in `kept`, unless it counts the name as a changeset or leaves it to `CacheScratch`. A changeset file is named as core names one, `pull-` or `range-` and 16 lowercase hex digits, with `.sqlite`, `-wal` or `-shm`; it and `scripted/` are never entries, and any other `.sqlite` name is listed. Under `graphs/`, `coverage/` and `mutation/`, prune skips only a name that `scratchName` in `cache-scratch.ts`, the test `CacheScratch` sweeps by, accepts. It never skips a link or an `entry-` name, which `CacheScratch` does not sweep. `open` strips `GIT_*` from the environment it runs git with, so a caller inside a git hook cannot point it at another repository. Refs under `refs/melian/pull/` hold no tree live: they outlive a merge, and the age bound spares a fork head reviewed that week.

verification.reason: The head adds a branch in `StorePrune.open` (store-prune.ts:186-187). A top-level `evidence` directory that isn't a link is measured into `evidence.bytes` and is not pushed to `kept`. The base had no `evidence` handling, so the directory fell through to `kept`. The guideline paragraph at pipeline.md:691 still says prune "lists every name it leaves in `kept`". It gives only two exceptions: changesets and names left to `CacheScratch`. A search of docs/ for `evidence/` or an evidence directory found nothing. The guideline never mentions the new `evidence` exemption or the `evidence` field on the plan, so it is stale and a reader would expect `evidence` in `kept`.
